quotes.text: we constructed a dataset containing nine core tables based on MIMIC-IV v3.1
extracted and filtered data from MIMIC-IV, mapping records to conform to our schema

rationale: Dataset name (MIMIC-IV), version (v3.1) and platform (PostgreSQL) are stated. No snapshot date, and no route from each task to its source MIMIC record (tasks are linked to 'clinically similar existing patients' and patient data synthesized with GPT-5). Calculator sources (MDCalc, Medscape, QxMD) carry no access date. Source named without a task-to-record route, so 1.

quotes.text: Patient data were derived from MIMIC-IV, a publicly available, de-identified dataset compliant with HIPAA regulations and approved by an institutional review board.
EHR data derived from MIMIC-IV and partially synthetic data

rationale: Origin (MIMIC-IV plus GPT-5-synthesized records), collection method (Stage III) and IRB/de-identification status of the source are stated. No licence or terms for the data are given: the README licence badge covers the repo only, and MIMIC-IV's own terms are not mentioned. Origin plus other elements but no licence, so 1 rather than 2.

quotes.text: selected patients with complete records across all tables, yielding a cohort of 49,419 patients

rationale: A sampling design is stated (patients with complete records across all nine tables; scenarios from a 125-category taxonomy). The Limitations section concedes region-specific bias. There is no comparison to a named target population, so 1.

searched: S1 (experiments, appendices B/C, Ethical Considerations), S2 (README), S3 (no chunks), S4/S5 (evaluation.py prompts, MCP servers). The Ethical Considerations text discusses risk in general terms, but no dedicated unsafe-output test or bias test is reported.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (none), S4 (tasks.jsonl, code), S5. No gating, canary, encryption, held-out set or overlap check is reported. Task files with calculator answers are released in the repo, and no contamination check is described.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (none), S4, S5. The README mentions a read-only DB user for 'secure query access', which concerns write safety, not isolation from ground truth. No statement says the agent cannot reach gold calculator answers or by what mechanism. Patient information is removed from task questions, which is a different matter.

quotes.text: a Google Search server with search and fetch tools for retrieving up-to-date medical references
we constructed a dataset containing nine core tables based on MIMIC-IV v3.1

rationale: The EHR database is built from a fixed MIMIC-IV v3.1 snapshot with a build script, so data is pinned. The agent tools include live Google Search (Serper API) and live page fetch, and the DeepSeek-V3.1 extractor has no snapshot or version pin beyond its name. Data pinned while a live service remains, so 1.

quotes.text: we referenced all elements against patient information through item-by-item review and correction

rationale: Solvability and correctness evidence is manual only: physician review of each task's calculators, outputs and inputs against patient data, plus exclusion of tasks lacking available calculators or EHR data. No scripted reference solution is run through the grader.

searched: S1 (tool descriptions in 3.2, A.3), S2 (README), S4/S5 (postgres_executor, python_executor, google_search servers). No task changes environment state: SQL runs in a READ ONLY transaction against a read-only DB user, and search, fetch and Python only return output. NA clause applies.

searched: S1 (metrics, Table 2, appendices), S2, S4/S5. No random or trivial-agent rate, chance rate per metric, or design argument against trivial success is reported. Task Fulfillment is near 100% for most models, but that concerns output validity, not chance-level scoring.
searched: S1 (Table 2, Table 3, appendices B), S2, S3 (none), S4. No do-nothing, random or trivial agent baseline is reported for any task.

quotes.text: we randomly sampled 20 tasks and re-ran the same extraction with GPT-5.2 under identical prompts

rationale: Appendix C.2 validates the DeepSeek-V3.1 result extractor on the benchmark's own trajectories with per-dimension agreement, Cohen's kappa, correlations and MAD (Tables 9 and 10). The reference is another LLM (GPT-5.2), not human labels, and the LLM calculator and SQL comparison step is not separately validated, so this is the weaker end of 2.

searched: S1 (A.1, A.3), S2 (README), S4 (llm.py, react.py, evaluation.py). S1 says only 'default hyperparameters unless otherwise specified' for closed models. No seed, temperature setting or repeated-run policy appears. Code retries on JSON or API failure (reliability, not determinism), so 0.

searched: S1 (Table 2, Section 4, appendices), S2, S4. Model comparisons are point estimates with no CI, SD or significance test. Kappa and correlation figures appear only for the extractor validation.

searched: S1 (4.1, A.1, A.3), S2 (README run instructions). No number of runs per task, seed or independence statement. 'Default hyperparameters unless otherwise specified' (closed models only) gives no actual decoding controls, so counted absent.
searched: S1 (Table 2 and appendices), S2, S4. No CI or SE on headline scores, no resampling unit, and no treatment of clustering of tasks within patients or scenarios.
searched: S1 (Table 3, B.2, B.3, B.4), S2, S3 (none), S4. No rerun, pass^k or action/state agreement information. Tool-usage counts are averages from a single run per model.

searched: S1 (Table 4, 4.1, A.1, A.3), S2, S3 (none), S4 (evaluation.py default 'claude-opus-4-5'). Models are given by name and version label (e.g. Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-5, Gemini-3-Pro-Preview), with no provider snapshot ID or date. No decoding parameters, and no harness commit or tag tied to the reported numbers. Only max rounds=80 is stated.

quotes.text: Execute a read-only SQL query on the PostgreSQL database.

rationale: A tool interface exists (three MCP servers, JSON action with server/tool/arguments). S1-S3 name the tools and indicate the SQL tool and DB user are read-only; read/write semantics for the other tools are not stated. No per-tool schema and no return or error semantics are documented in S1-S3; those appear only in code (typed signatures, error-string returns). The read-only property reaches the agent through the tool docstring. The paper names the tool run_sql while code and README use run_read_only_sql.

quotes.text: Expected output shows successful tool execution for all three servers:

rationale: The README provides an --mcp_test smoke check of all three servers, which counts as a conformance check. No statement about simulated, stubbed or no-op behaviour appears in S1-S3, and S1 does not say nothing is simulated. The Python executor blocks certain keywords with a Security Error that is not described in S1-S3. S5 reach cannot be determined.

searched: S1 (3.2 tools), S2, S4/S5 (postgres_executor, python_executor, google_search servers). All tools are read or compute only: SQL runs as a READ ONLY transaction, and search, fetch and Python return output. No action mutates environment state or represents a clinical order, prescription, note or message, so the NA clause applies.

quotes.text: extract the final calculator names, numerical results, and retrieved SQL fields into a standardized JSON format for automated evaluation
Beyond final-answer accuracy, MedMCP-Calc assesses the information acquisition phase by analyzing database interactions

rationale: Grader input is named: the agent's trajectory and final answer, parsed by DeepSeek-V3.1 and compared with ground truth by an LLM. A rationale for trajectory-based process evaluation is given, and tasks involve no environment end state. The extractor validation (20 tasks, agreement with GPT-5.2, no per-class error rates, no human labels or injected outcomes) does not meet element (iii), so 1.

searched: S1, S2, S3 (none), S4 (tasks.jsonl), S5. No leakage controls: the agent has live Google Search and fetch, and the same calculator sites serve as ground-truth references. No held-out or private split is described, task files are in the repo, and there is no canary or provenance marker.

quotes.text: Performance varies across clinical domains, with all models achieving higher scores in Critical Care & Perioperative Medicine

rationale: Table 2 reports CS, EA and QP per clinical domain, a named benchmark axis. The source database holds demographic fields (gender, birth_date, ethnicity, nationality) but no per-patient-subgroup results are reported. No per-domain test task counts appear in S1 (appendix counts are for the training set only).

quotes.text: synthesized corresponding patient data with GPT-5
Patient data were derived from MIMIC-IV, a publicly available, de-identified dataset compliant with HIPAA regulations and approved by an institutional review board.

rationale: Source is stated as mixed: de-identified MIMIC-IV plus task-specific records synthesized with GPT-5 (the README says 'partially synthetic'). Governance is stated (de-identified, HIPAA, IRB). No data terms or redistribution conditions are given separately from the code's MIT licence badge, so element (iii) is absent.
